title: Personalize at Test Time: Learning User Preferences for Image Generation
title_zh: 测试时的个性化：学习图像生成的用户偏好

paragraphs.en: Diffusion models can generate high-quality images, yet aligning their outputs with individual user preferences remains challenging. A key bottleneck is accurately modeling diverse user preferences from limited feedback. Existing approaches often rely on labor-intensive manual preference annotations or vision-language models(VLM) to extract preference information from user interaction histories, introducing substantial annotation or computational costs that limit scalability. We propose an approach that learns personalized reward models directly from users’ historical image preference pairs. First, we use an autoencoder to compress hundreds of visual attributes into 50 attribute-anchored preference dimensions and train an evaluator to score images along these dimensions. We then represent each user’s preferences as a linear combination of the shared dimension scores, estimating the user-specific weights by maximizing the likelihood of their observed pairwise preferences under the Bradley–Terry model. This formulation reduces per-user adaptation to optimizing a low-dimensional weight vector, simplifying optimization and enabling data-efficient personalization from sparse feedback. The learned personalized rewards guide image generation at inference time while keeping the diffusion model frozen. Experiments on real-user preference data show that our approach achieves approximately 77% held-out pairwise preference prediction accuracy and improves the alignment of generated images with individual user preferences.

paragraphs.en: Text-to-image diffusion models have made remarkable progress in visual fidelity, prompt adherence, and compositional generation, powering increasingly capable systems such as Stable Diffusion ( Podell et al., 2024 ; Rombach et al., 2022 ) , DALL-E ( Ramesh et al., 2021 ) , and Seedream ( Seedream et al., 2025 ) . These approaches have proven effective for applications including subject-driven generation, style customization, and general preference alignment.

paragraphs.en: Despite their effectiveness in many applications, personalizing diffusion models to individual users remains challenging, as it requires accurately modeling each user’s preferences from limited feedback. Existing approaches generally obtain user preferences in two ways: using vision-language models to summarize a user’s historical preference records into a profile or embedding ( Dang et al., 2025 ; Kim et al., 2025a ) , or collecting explicit human annotations of users’ likes and dislikes and converting them into structured visual preferences to guide generation ( Salehi et al., 2024 ) . These approaches have two important limitations. First, incorporating preference representations requires additional fine-tuning of the diffusion model or training of a specialized adapter, introducing substantial computational cost and limiting scalability across different generative models. Second, acquiring reliable preference representations remains difficult: profiles inferred by vision-language models may be inaccurate when user histories are short, long, or heterogeneous, while collecting detailed human annotations imposes considerable burden on users.

paragraphs.en: In this work, we propose PAT( P ersonalized a t T est Time for diffusion models), which instantiates a personalized reward model at test time directly from a user’s historical preference feedback. For each pair of images generated for a prompt, a user only needs to indicate which image they prefer. Our approach assumes that user preferences admit a low-dimensional latent representation, with individual differences captured by the weights each user assigns to shared preference dimensions. We therefore formulate personalization as a two-stage problem: first, identifying a compact, shared visual attribute space that captures diverse preference-relevant attributes; and second, quantifying each user’s preferences along these dimensions. To identify the shared preference dimensions, we draw on the collection of over 500 visual attributes compiled by Salehi et al. (2024) . While these attributes provide broad coverage of visual preferences, estimating a separate weight for every attribute would require fitting hundreds of user-specific parameters from only a small number of pairwise observations, making preference estimation prone to overfitting. We therefore seek a compact shared representation that preserves meaningful variation across visual attributes while reducing the number of parameters to be estimated for each user. To this end, we use an autoencoder to derive a low-dimensional set of shared preference dimensions grounded in these attributes. Unlike covariance-based linear methods such as PCA ( Pearson, 1901 ; Hotelling, 1933 ) and factor analysis ( Spearman, 1961 ; Thurstone, 1931 ) , the autoencoder can capture a nonlinear low-dimensional representation that better preserves interactions among visual attributes. paragraphs.en: A growing body of work aligns pretrained diffusion models with downstream objectives such as human preferences, aesthetic quality, and safety-awareness. One class of approaches fine-tunes the diffusion model using reward supervision, thereby incorporating the desired objective into the model parameters ( Dai et al., 2023 ; Betker et al., 2023 ; Clark et al., 2023 ; Prabhudesai et al., 2023 ; Fan et al., 2023 ; Black et al., 2023 ) . Another class performs alignment at inference time, steering the denoising trajectory or directly optimizing the latent variables while keeping the pretrained diffusion model frozen ( Jiang et al., 2026 ; Goyal et al., 2026 ; Tang et al., 2024 ; Yeh et al., 2024 ; Kim et al., ; Zhai et al., 2025 ) . More recently, reinforcement learning has been introduced to diffusion model alignment by treating denoising as a sequential decision-making process. Existing methods employ policy-optimization algorithms such as GRPO ( Zheng et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026 ; Xue et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025a ; Li et al., 2025b ; Li et al., 2026c ) , as well as RLHF and direct preference optimization objectives such as DPO ( Wallace et al., 2024 ; Jiang et al., 2026 ; Liang et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2025 ; Lee et al., 2025b ; Gu et al., 2024 ; Yang et al., 2024a ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) , to improve generation according to human feedback or learned rewards. While most of these methods perform alignment by updating the diffusion model during training, a small number of concurrent works, besides ours, have also explored alignment at inference time. Jin et al. (2025) and Xie et al. (2026) investigate training-free inference-time reward transfer from RL aligned-base difference between tuned model and base model. Chen et al. (2026) treats intermediate flow latents as implicit policies and optimizes them at test time using PRDP and GRPO objectives.

paragraphs.en: Personalization has been extensively studied for large language models through approaches such as user-profile conditioning, memory augmentation, parameter-efficient adaptation, and personalized reward modeling ( Yang et al., 2024b ; Li et al., 2026a ; Poddar et al., 2024 ; Wang et al., 2024 ; Song et al., 2026 ; Yu et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026a ; Wu et al., 2026 ; Tan et al., 2026 ; Barreto et al., 2025 ; Cai et al., 2026 ; Iyer et al., ; Chen et al., 2025 ; Shenfeld et al., 2025 ; Kim et al., 2025b ) . Personalizing diffusion models poses additional challenges. An LLM can jointly interpret heterogeneous user histories, extract preference-relevant information, and incorporate the resulting profile into generation through natural-language conditioning. In contrast, a diffusion model primarily serves as a generator and does not natively provide a comparable interface for reasoning over user histories or constructing explicit user models. Existing approaches therefore commonly rely on external vision-language models to summarize a user’s prior choices or encode them into preference representations, while others use human-defined attributes or manual annotations to characterize the relevant dimensions of variation ( Dang et al., 2025 ; Lee et al., 2025a ; Salehi et al., 2024 ; Kim et al., 2025a ; Wang et al., 2026b ; Li et al., 2026b ) . Our approach makes diffusion personalization more scalable by directly learning shared preference dimensions and user-specific rewards from pairwise feedback. It requires neither external VLM-based nor manual analysis of each user’s history, and personalizes generation at inference time without fine-tuning the underlying diffusion model.
paragraphs.zh: 针对大型语言模型的个性化方法已得到广泛研究，包括用户画像条件约束、记忆增强、参数高效自适应以及个性化奖励建模等方法（Yang et al., 2024b；Li et al., 2026a；Poddar et al., 2024；Wang et al., 2024；Song et al., 2026；Yu et al., 2026；Wang et al., 2026a；Wu et al., 2026；Tan et al., 2026；Barreto et al., 2025；Cai et al., 2026；Iyer et al.；Chen et al., 2025；Shenfeld et al., 2025；Kim et al., 2025b）。 对扩散模型进行个性化则带来了额外的挑战。 大型语言模型能够联合解析异构的用户历史，提取与偏好相关的信息，并通过自然语言条件约束将生成的用户画像融入生成过程。 相比之下，扩散模型主要充当生成器，其本身并不提供可用于推理用户历史或构建显式用户模型的类似接口。 因此，现有方法通常依赖外部的视觉-语言模型来总结用户的过往选择或将其编码为偏好表示，而另一些方法则使用人工定义的属性或手动标注来刻画相关变化维度（Dang et al., 2025；Lee et al., 2025a；Salehi et al., 2024；Kim et al., 2025a；Wang et al., 2026b；Li et al., 2026b）。 我们的方法通过直接从成对反馈中学习共享的偏好维度和用户特定的奖励，使扩散模型的个性化更具可扩展性。 该方法既不需要基于外部视觉-语言模型的分析，也不需要手动分析每个用户的历史，并能在推理阶段实现个性化生成，而无需对底层的扩散模型进行微调。

paragraphs.en: We construct the data for learning the shared preference evaluator from the training split of Pick-a-Pic v1 ( Kirstain et al., 2023 ) , where each comparison consists of a text prompt c c , two generated images ( x + , x − ) (x^{+},x^{-}) , and the image preferred by the user. We sample a dimension-learning pool of 50,000 images from light raters. To obtain structured supervision describing the visual properties of each image, we annotate the pool with Qwen2.5-VL-72B ( Bai et al., 2025 ) using the ViPer attribute taxonomy ( Salehi et al., 2024 ) . The taxonomy contains approximately 512 attributes organized into 21 visual categories, including art style, color palette, composition, and mood. paragraphs.en: Our experiments evaluate two central questions: (1) whether the learned personalized reward accurately represents a user’s preferences, and (2) whether this reward can be used to generate images that match those preferences. We first study a controlled toy setting with manually specified synthetic preference profiles, and then extend the evaluation to real user preferences from Pick-a-Pic.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的实验评估了两个核心问题：（1）所学习到的个性化奖励是否准确反映了用户的偏好，以及（2）这种奖励能否用于生成符合这些偏好的图像。 我们首先在一个受控的简化环境中进行研究，其中合成偏好配置文件是手动指定的，然后将评估扩展到来自 Pick-a-Pic 的真实用户偏好。

paragraphs.en: We begin with a controlled toy experiment involving five synthetic users, each represented by a manually specified ground-truth preference vector λ ⋆ \lambda^{\star} (Table 5 ). Their preferences are defined over five candidate reward dimensions: clip ( Radford et al., 2021 ) , aes ( Schuhmann, 2022 ) , color ( Hasler and Suesstrunk, 2003 ) , hps ( Wu et al., 2023 ) , and pickscore ( Kirstain et al., 2023 ) . These scores capture complementary aspects of visual appearance and text–image alignment; details are provided in Appendix B.1 . We repeat the experiment three times, sampling 200 captioned image pairs from Pick-a-Pic v1 in each repetition and splitting them into 100 training and 100 test pairs. After standardizing each reward dimension over the sampled images, we construct synthetic preference labels by selecting the image with the higher ground-truth weighted reward, ( λ ⋆ ) ⊤ ​ r ​ ( c , x ) (\lambda^{\star})^{\top}r(c,x) . We then estimate λ \lambda from the training preferences by maximizing the Bradley–Terry likelihood with regularization 0.1. Evaluation considers the preference prediction accuracy on the held-out pairs. We compare the learned multi-dimensional reward with the ground-truth reward and a best one-hot baseline, which uses the highest-performing individual reward dimension available in each configuration. This comparison tests whether learning a combination of reward signals better captures a user’s preferences than relying on a single evaluator.

We evaluate 631 users, holding out 50 preference pairs per user for testing and using their remaining pairs for training. To examine performance under different amounts of personal feedback, we groups users by their training-set sizes, with 66, 55, 120, and 390 users in the four groups, respectively. paragraphs.en: Table 2 shows that PAT achieves strong preference prediction performance across different amounts of user feedback. Personalization provides substantial gains: compared with using shared population-level weights, user-specific modeling improves accuracy by 5.5 % 5.5\% – 7.9 % 7.9\% across all four groups, highlighting the importance of capturing individual preferences. Mixed-effects modeling is particularly useful when feedback is limited: it improves accuracy by 1.1 % 1.1\% and 0.7 % 0.7\% percentage points in the 20–30 and 30–60 groups, respectively, while matching independent fitting in the smallest group. Alternating training further improves accuracy across all groups, supporting joint adaptation of the evaluator and user-specific weights.

paragraphs.en: We compare the autoencoder with two linear dimension reduction methods:(a) a correlation-based baseline that groups correlated visual attributes and averages their binary labels to construct shared preference dimensions and (b) Principle Component Analysis(PCA) that uses SVD to factorize the binary label matrix and use the top k k principle dimension as shared preference dimensions. paragraphs.en: We evaluate whether the learned personalized rewards improve image generation beyond ranking existing images. We include all 631 users and generate 10 images per user for each method. We use Stable Diffusion 3.5 (SD3.5) as the base generator, with 30 sampling steps and a classifier-free guidance scale of 4.5. For PAT, we optimize the initial noise using Direct Noise Optimization (DNO) with the learned personalized reward, while keeping the diffusion model frozen. DNO runs for 30 optimization steps with a learning rate of 0.005. We use GPT-5.5 as the judge under a blind, profile-aware evaluation protocol, comparing each method’s outputs against vanilla SD3.5 for alignment with the user’s preferences. latex We first provide GPT-5.5 with 10 image pairs and the user’s recorded preferences, one pair for each test prompt, to construct a user preference profile. We then use this profile to guide GPT-5.5 in judging which generated image better aligns with the user’s preferences. The prompt templates are provided in Appendix C .
paragraphs.zh: 我们评估所学习的个性化奖励在超越现有图像排序方面，是否提升了图像生成效果。 我们纳入了全部 631 名用户，并为每种方法为每位用户生成 10 张图像。 我们将 Stable Diffusion 3.5（SD3.5）用作基础生成器，设置 30 次采样步骤和无分类器引导尺度为 4.5。 对于 PAT，我们使用直接噪声优化（DNO）结合所学习的个性化奖励来优化初始噪声，同时保持扩散模型冻结不变。 DNO 运行 30 次优化步骤，学习率为 0.005。 在盲测且考虑用户画像的评估协议下，我们使用 GPT-5.5 作为评判者，将每种方法的输出与原始 SD3.5 进行比较，以评估其与用户偏好的契合度。首先，我们为 GPT-5.5 提供 10 对图像和用户的记录偏好，每个测试提示词对应一对图像，从而构建用户偏好画像。 随后，我们利用该画像指导 GPT-5.5 判断哪张生成的图像更符合用户的偏好。 提示词模板见附录 C。

paragraphs.en: We compare against our reproduction of Personalized Preference Fine-tuning of Diffusion Models (PPD). For each user, PPD randomly selects four historical prompt–image pairs and uses a 72B Qwen vision-language model to extract the user’s preferences. The resulting VLM embeddings serve as additional conditioning signals for diffusion model fine-tuning, and the texts summarized from VLM are treated as user profile. At generation time, we set PPD’s user-signal guidance scale to 1. We also include a Profile-as-Prompt baseline, which appends the textual user profile produced by PPD’s VLM to the original generation prompt, directly conditioning SD3.5 on the preference description.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将结果与自己对“扩散模型个性化偏好微调”（PPD）方法的复现进行比较。 对于每个用户，PPD 会随机选择四个历史提示–图像对，并使用一个 72B 的 Qwen 视觉语言模型来提取用户的偏好。 由此得到的 VLM 嵌入将作为扩散模型微调的额外条件信号，而从 VLM 中总结出的文本则被用作用户画像。 在生成阶段，我们将 PPD 的用户信号引导尺度设为 1。 我们还加入了一个“画像即提示”的基线方法：该方法会将 PPD 的 VLM 生成的文本用户画像附加到原始生成提示中，从而直接对 SD3.5 施加偏好描述的约束。

paragraphs.en: To assess whether the personalized generation gains reflect a general improvement in image quality, we compare PAT with vanilla SD3.5 over the image pairs generated from the same prompts. We evaluate each pair using four general-purpose quality and alignment metrics: PickScore, HPS, CLIP, and AES. paragraphs.en: We introduced PAT, a framework for personalizing diffusion models at test time from historical pairwise preferences. By combining shared, attribute-grounded reward dimensions with user-specific weights, PAT enables preference estimation from limited feedback and guides generation while keeping the diffusion model frozen. Experiments demonstrate improved preference prediction and better personalized generation win rate over vanilla SD3.5, without consistent gains in generic quality metrics. These results support compact personalized rewards as an effective interface between individual preferences and inference-time image generation.

paragraphs.en: This work uses existing public preference data from Pick-a-Pic and involves no new participant recruitment or manual preference annotation. Automated visual attribute annotations and model-based generation evaluations may reflect biases in the underlying models and data. Personalized generation may reinforce biased preferences or produce harmful content, while user histories and learned preference vectors may reveal sensitive information. Practical deployment should therefore protect preference data and retain appropriate content-safety safeguards.

paragraphs.en: CLIP ( Radford et al., 2021 ) learns a shared image–text embedding space through contrastive training on image–text pairs. We use the similarity between the embeddings of a generated image and its corresponding prompt to measure semantic alignment. Higher scores indicate stronger correspondence between the image content and the text description. This dimension captures prompt relevance, although it does not directly measure visual quality or individual user preferences.
paragraphs.zh: CLIP（Radford 等人，2021）通过图像-文本对的对比训练，学习到一个共享的图像-文本嵌入空间。 我们利用生成图像与其对应提示词嵌入之间的相似度来衡量语义对齐程度。 分数越高，表示图像内容与文本描述之间的对应关系越强。 该维度捕捉了提示词的相关性，但并不直接衡量视觉质量或个体用户的偏好。

This dimension captures visual appeal that may not be reflected by text–image similarity alone.

paragraphs.en: The colorfulness metric of Hasler and Suesstrunk (2003) quantifies image colorfulness using statistics of red–green and yellow–blue opponent channels. It combines the variability and mean magnitude of these color signals to produce an image-only score. Unlike the learned reward models, this metric measures a specific visual property without preference supervision. Higher values indicate more colorful images, which need not be preferred by every user; its contribution to the synthetic reward is determined by the user’s weight vector.
paragraphs.zh: Hasler 和 Suesstrunk（2003）提出的色彩丰富度指标通过红-绿和黄-蓝对立通道的统计量来量化图像的色彩丰富度。 该指标结合这些颜色信号的变异性与平均幅度，生成一个仅基于图像的得分。 与学习型奖励模型不同，该指标无需偏好监督即可测量特定的视觉属性。 数值越高表示图像越富有色彩，但这并不一定意味着所有用户都会偏好此类图像；其对合成奖励的贡献由用户的权重向量决定。

paragraphs.en: Human Preference Score v2 ( Wu et al., 2023 ) is a CLIP-based scoring model fine-tuned on the Human Preference Dataset v2 (HPD v2). Given a prompt and an image, it predicts a score intended to reflect human preferences over generated images. Compared with the original CLIP similarity, this score incorporates explicit human preference supervision and provides a broader signal of perceived image quality and prompt compatibility.

paragraphs.en: PickScore ( Kirstain et al., 2023 ) is a CLIP-based preference model trained on pairwise human feedback from Pick-a-Pic. It assigns a scalar score to a prompt–image pair using the scaled similarity between its learned text and image embeddings. Training encourages the relative scores of competing images to match observed human choices. Like HPS, PickScore provides a population-level preference signal; the two models are trained on different preference datasets and may therefore rank the same images differently.

paragraphs.en: Pick-a-Pic ( Kirstain et al., 2023 ) is an open dataset of real user preferences for text-to-image generation, collected through a web application in which users submit prompts and compare generated images. Each comparison associates a text prompt with two candidate images and the user’s preference feedback. The dataset also permits ties and includes user identifiers, enabling preference observations to be grouped into individual user histories. Its prompts and judgments arise from users interacting with image generation systems, providing a setting for studying heterogeneous visual preferences.
paragraphs.zh: Pick-a-Pic（Kirstain 等人，2023）是一个开放数据集，包含真实用户对文本到图像生成任务的偏好数据。这些数据通过一个网页应用收集，用户在该应用中提交提示词并比较生成的图像。 每次比较都将一个文本提示词与两张候选图像以及用户的偏好反馈关联起来。 该数据集也允许出现平票情况，并包含用户标识符，从而可以将偏好观察结果按单个用户的历史记录进行分组。 其中的提示词和判断均源于用户与图像生成系统的互动，为研究异质性视觉偏好提供了实际场景。

paragraphs.en: We use Pick-a-Pic v1 in two experimental settings. In the controlled toy experiments, it supplies captioned image pairs, while preference labels are constructed from the synthetic weighted reward rather than the original human choices. Each repetition samples 200 pairs, with 100 used for fitting the preference weights and 100 for evaluation. In the real-user experiments, we use the recorded human choices to fit and evaluate personalized rewards. Following Section 4.2, we select the 631 users with the largest numbers of preference pairs from the training split, hold out 50 pairs per user for evaluation, and use the remaining pairs for training. These experiments assess, respectively, recovery of controlled synthetic preferences and prediction of unseen choices from real users.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在两种实验设置中使用 Pick-a-Pic v1。 在受控的玩具实验中，它提供带标题的图片对，而偏好标签则基于合成的加权奖励构建，而非原始的人类选择。 每次重复会采样 200 对图片，其中 100 对用于拟合偏好权重，另外 100 对用于评估。 在真实用户实验中，我们使用记录的人类选择来拟合和评估个性化奖励。 遵循第 4.2 节的流程，我们从训练集中选出偏好对数量最多的 631 名用户，为每位用户保留 50 对图片用于评估，其余图片则用于训练。 这些实验分别评估了受控合成偏好的恢复能力，以及对真实用户未观察到的选择进行预测的能力。

paragraphs.en: Table 5 reports the ground-truth and fitted preference weights for the five synthetic users introduced in Section 4.1 , with fitted weights averaged over three independently sampled datasets. The configurations cover both broadly distributed preferences (uniform and half-normal) and more concentrated preferences (Pareto). Weight recovery is strongest for the heavy-1 configuration, with a reported cosine similarity of 0.990, and the fitted vector preserves its emphasis on the third and fourth reward dimensions. Recovery is less accurate for the uniform and half-normal configurations, where the fitted weights place greater emphasis on the fifth dimension. These results highlight that recovering the exact preference weights remains challenging with limited pairwise feedback, even in this controlled setting.
paragraphs.zh: 表 5 报告了第 4.1 节中介绍的五个合成用户的真实偏好权重和拟合出的偏好权重，其中拟合权重是在三个独立采样的数据集上取平均得到的。 这些配置涵盖了广泛分布的偏好（均匀分布和半正态分布）以及更为集中的偏好（帕累托分布）。 在 heavy-1 配置中，权重的恢复效果最佳，报告余弦相似度为 0.990，且拟合向量保留了其对第三和第四奖励维度的侧重。 在均匀分布和半正态分布配置中，恢复的准确性较低，此时拟合权重对第五维度的重视程度更高。 这些结果表明，即使在受控环境中，当成对反馈有限时，恢复精确的偏好权重仍然具有挑战性。

paragraphs.en: Table 7 presents the two-stage prompting protocol used for profile-aware evaluation. First, GPT-5.5 constructs a user preference profile from 10 image pairs, one for each test prompt. Within each pair, the preferred image is followed by the dispreferred image, allowing the model to summarize both favored and rejected visual characteristics. The profile covers subject matter and stylistic preferences while explicitly excluding judgments of image quality or rendering fidelity. Second, GPT-5.5 receives this profile, an evaluation caption, and two generated images, and selects the image that better matches the user’s preferences. In the templates, {k} and {n} are set to 10 and 20, respectively; {profile} and {caption} are replaced with the generated profile and evaluation caption.
paragraphs.zh: 表7展示了用于基于用户画像评估的两阶段提示协议。 首先，GPT-5.5根据每组测试提示中的10对图像构建用户偏好画像，每对图像对应一个测试提示。 在每一对图像中，首选图像之后是次选图像，这使得模型能够总结受青睐和被拒绝的视觉特征。 该画像涵盖了主题内容和风格偏好，但明确排除了对图像质量或渲染保真度的判断。 其次，GPT-5.5接收该画像、评估说明以及两张生成的图像，并选择更符合用户偏好的图像。 在模板中，{k}和{n}分别设置为10和20；{profile}和{caption}则被替换为生成的画像和评估说明。

paragraphs.en: We apply Direct Noise Optimization (DNO) ( Tang et al., 2024 ) to maximize the learned personalized reward at inference time while keeping the image generator frozen. Stable Diffusion 3.5 uses a flow-matching model with a deterministic ODE-based sampler in our implementation. Once the prompt, initial latent, and sampling configuration are fixed, no additional randomness is introduced during denoising. Consequently, the complete generation process can be represented as a deterministic mapping
paragraphs.zh: 我们在推理阶段应用直接噪声优化（DNO）（Tang 等人，2024），以最大化所学习的个性化奖励，同时保持图像生成器冻结。 在我们的实现中，Stable Diffusion 3.5 使用了一个基于确定性常微分方程的采样器的流匹配模型。 一旦提示词、初始潜在变量和采样配置确定后，在去噪过程中就不会引入任何额外的随机性。 因此，整个生成过程可以表示为一个确定性映射。
